title: Pannwitz's bound on unit-distance pairs in a set of diameter one
statement: Let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be points of the Euclidean plane $\bbr^2$ whose set $\{x_1, \dots, x_n\}$ has diameter exactly $1$. Then the number of unordered pairs $\{i, j\}$ with $i \ne j$ and $\dist(x_i, x_j) = 1$ is at most $n$; equivalently, the unit-distance graph on these points has at most $n$ edges.
hypotheses_covered: n points x_1,...,x_n in the Euclidean plane
the point set has diameter exactly 1
replaced:
